beats.text: This is how a new player keeps their cash, keeps their cars and stays off the police radar. Here is the first problem. The cash in your pocket is gone when you die. Here is the second. The cops remember your face and your outfit.

beats.text: Tip number one, and it is the most important tip in this whole video. Bank your cash. Whatever you carry is lost when you die. Guides say the same goes for getting busted. I had five hundred and thirty-one dollars on me on launch night. One plane crash and one shootout later, my HUD said zero. Guides also report a small fee from your BuckMe bank app when you go down. So every time you pass an ATM with real money on you, stop and deposit it. Cash in the bank survives. Cash in your pocket is only on loan. Every robbery fills your pocket. So bank it before the next one.

beats.text: Tip number two. You deposit at an ATM, in person. A lot of new players think the phone app can bank their cash. It cannot. Guides agree your phone will not move pocket cash into the bank. ATMs sit in places you already visit. Lucia's motel has one in the lobby. The convenience store has one by the magazines. Find the ATM before you find the action.

beats.text: Tip number three. Jason and Lucia share one bank account. I spent a pile of Jason's bank money at Coastal Auto Care. Later, Lucia checked her ATM, and those charges were on her statement, with Brian's payments too. So money one of them banks is money the other one can spend.

beats.text: Tip number four. Stolen goods are not money yet. When you loot narcotics, jewelry or marked bills, they go into a stash bag. The game tells you straight. Take them to a drop-off to sell for usable cash. Early on, that drop-off is Brian's Lockup. Look for the blue building with the marlin mural. Carry the bag inside. Inside, the sell prompt offered eight thousand one hundred and sixty dollars for my stash. Until someone pays you, that bag is just a heavy backpack.

beats.text: Tip number five. Stow that stash bag in your vehicle, and sell it soon. At your car, you can stow the bag or keep it on your back. Guides warn that a bag on your back will most likely be lost if you go down. So loot, stow, and drive straight to the drop-off. Do not go sightseeing with a bag of jewelry. And once Brian pays, the money lands straight in your bank account. A death cannot touch it there.

beats.text: Tip number six. Small stores pay small money, and the game shuts them after. At Tucker's farm stand, someone else was already holding the place up. I stopped him. The clerk told me to take whatever I wanted, and I walked off with about a hundred dollars. Right after, the game told me Tucker's Citrus Farms was closed due to a robbery. The game also tells you that you can mug people, and rob places with your partner. I robbed a pawn shop myself, and it turned into a shootout. So rob small, bank it, and keep moving.

beats.text: Tip number seven. The police remember what you look like. Open the map after a crime and read the search area. When my stars went up, two red icons showed under them, a clothes hanger and a person. Guides say those mean outfit known and appearance known. Check them every time the stars go up. So hiding is only half the job. You also have to stop looking like you. In Leonida, your outfit is evidence.

beats.text: Tip number eight. To lose the cops, break line of sight, then leave the red zone. The red area on your map is where they are searching. Get out of it, and do not drive back in. Here is a myth to drop. Stars gone does not mean you are safe. Look at my screen here. The stars are gone from my HUD. But the map still shows the search zone, and it still knows my outfit. Guides agree the hot area stays while the heat fades. If police spot you there, the stars come back. So keep heading away from that zone. Leave like you have somewhere better to be.

beats.text: Tip number nine. When you cannot outrun them, hide. Crouch in bushes, or behind a shipping container or a dumpster. Then stay hidden until the search moves past. Lucia crept through the bushes beside a waterfront restaurant like this, with four stars still up. One catch. Guides say that if police dogs show up, you should keep moving, or they will hunt you down. Out of sight is the goal.

beats.text: Tip number ten. Change your outfit, but only once you are out of sight. Guides say a new outfit clears the outfit known line on your map. But that only works once you have broken line of sight. Lucia slipped away in a tow truck, with the stars still flashing. Only once the stars were gone did she walk into a clothing store. Denim cutoffs were twelve dollars. That is a cheap disguise. Three separate guides also suggest keeping a spare outfit in your car's trunk. Change after you vanish, never before.

beats.text: Tip number eleven. Small changes throw off the description too. Hats and glasses sit on the items wheel, so you can swap them in a second. Guides also say splitting up Jason and Lucia helps, because the police note your partner as well. A cap costs a lot less than getting busted.

beats.text: Tip number twelve. The Pay 'n' Spray trick from older games does not work here. The game says you cannot enter a Pay 'n' Spray when the cops are nearby or chasing you. Lose them first. Then respray the car. The respray menu says a new color reduces recognition. At Moses' shop, a respray was a hundred dollars. So the order is always the same. Escape first, then paint. Paint hides the car. It does not hide you.

beats.text: Tip number thirteen. Check a car before you steal it. Scan a parked car with the WAiNK app, and a panel shows its lock, its alarm and its tracker. The game also says Focus shows if there is anything valuable in the trunk. At Moses's yard, I scanned a Vapid Montagne XL. Locked, alarmed, tracker none. No tracker is what matters. That is the one you want. Locked cars open with a Slim Jim, and Moses teaches you how.

beats.text: Tip number seventeen. Sell your spare untracked cars to Moses. Pull into his shop, hold the button, and sell. Moses offered me three hundred and fifty dollars for a Bravado Bogan. Guides say that money goes straight into your bank, so no ATM run is needed. But read his rule first. Moses will not take a car you stole close by. So grab one across town, then drive it in.

beats.text: Tip number twenty. Save your adrenaline for emergencies. The tooltip says adrenaline boosts your health, stamina and focus all at once, for a short time. That makes it your panic button. Use it when your health is low and you cannot get to cover. Do not waste a panic button on a jog.

beats.text: Tip number twenty-one. Work out, finish the full set, then rest. The strength workouts have a rep counter, like thirteen out of fifteen pull-ups. See it through to the end. Jason's level went up the moment his session said workout complete. His workout reached level three of four. After a session, the game tells you that you need time to recover. So train, go do a job, and come back later.

Its pins also explain what each place is for, like Brian's Lockup and the mod shop. When the game says map updated, open it and look. A lot of this guide is written right there on that map.

beats.text: Tip number twenty-seven. This is the third way to lose your stuff that I promised you. Anything you do not own, or did not store, is gone when you load back in. The game says it plainly. Unowned vehicles, weapons or items you did not store during your last session were lost. I saw that warning when I loaded back into Jason's house. The game warns that unowned weapons are lost when you die in combat or get arrested. So treat guns you pick up off the floor as temporary. Guides say guns you buy are yours to keep. Cars work the same way. If a car is not registered, it is not yours. Own it, store it, or say goodbye to it.
